items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I mean you heard it all the time with Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: But it’s definitely not a technical thing. I mean you have to have enough technique to convey, to be able to manifest this thing that’s happening, but technique is — nothing against technique — but it has to be up to a certain level but it’s definitely not a technical thing.

I mean you hear Trane, I’m aware of the feeling. I’m not aware of the amazing chops that he had to do it. It’s like you hear a man really playing from his soul. I mean to me, it’s like any of the great players I hear, whatever technical brilliance they have, you never lose the blues. The blues is always somehow there in any of the people that you dig. I mean you heard it all the time with Louis Armstrong. You hear it with Billie Holiday. You hear it with Trane. You hear it with Sonny. You hear it with somebody…
